review: Independent source review of the separate native-build fix; earlier review receipts preserved
scope: ios/Timbre/Audio/AudioService.swift: suspend and stopMetronome cancellation additions
assessment: The prior source approval did not establish native compilation. The subsequently reported hosted errors show that two actual Earcons call sites were missed by that earlier review; this receipt does not rewrite that evidence or describe the prior build as passing.

Full repository rg search over *.swift found five actual prepareInterfaceSound calls, all awaited: SoundFX initialization and playback preparation, Earcons default preparation dependency, and two AudioStartupTests calls. The function declaration is the sixth search match. No remaining synchronous call was found.

Earcons caches a closure retaining an unprepared AVAudioPlayer. The real player factory does not prepare or play. The playback closure calls prepareToPlay/currentTime/play only after InterfaceSoundPlayback finishes awaited session preparation and enters its contiguous MainActor action.

Inside that action, Task cancellation, enabled state, take generation, newest request within the channel and monotonic age in 0...0.15 seconds are rechecked before touching the player. A delayed, disabled, superseded or cancelled cue is discarded. Judgment and multiplier channels are distinct, so same-update hit and tier feedback do not cancel one another.

AudioService.suspend covers global stop and interruption suspension; stopMetronome also invalidates queued Earcons feedback. Their cancellation calls execute on MainActor, so a pending cue action cannot interleave between generation invalidation and the surrounding synchronous stop operation. Already playing sounds are not stopped by cancelPending, consistent with its pending-feedback purpose.

The seven tests use controlled preparation continuations and a fake monotonic clock, exercising the actual Earcons request path rather than arithmetic-only state. They meaningfully cover preparation ordering, disable-after-wait, same-channel replacement, stale age, generation cancellation, task cancellation and independent note/tier channels.

The explicit MainActor function types, injected constructor dependencies, defaults and returned player closures are internally consistent by source inspection. No high-confidence Swift type/actor defect was identified, but these declarations and XCTest cases still require the real Swift 5.10 strict-concurrency compiler.

begin.advanced(by: .seconds(cycle)) preserves advancement from the prior absolute instant; it does not re-anchor the musical clock to the current wall time. It removes the exact newly reported shorthand_operator source form.
